Job Posting: Environmental Scientist

Delta Stewardship Council

JC-525875



Environmental Scientist
  
ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST

$4,551.00 - $9,787.00 per Month
  
New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**Final Filing Date:** **11/30/2026**

### **Job Description and Duties**

**Telework Information:** Hybrid approach that includes office- and remote-centric work solutions.
  
  
Per CCR 249.3 this job control may be used to fill subsequent vacancies.

Do you want to be a part of a dynamic team of highly motivated individuals who enjoy working to benefit present and future generations of Californians? Join the Delta Stewardship Council, where we ensure a more reliable California water supply and a resilient Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta ecosystem while protecting and enhancing the region as a special place where people live, work, and recreate!

In this position, you will perform scientific research that directly supports the Delta Independent Science Board's (Delta ISB) reviews of the scientific research, monitoring, and assessment programs that inform adaptive management of the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta. Your research will involve literature reviews and syntheses obtained from workshops, interviews and surveys with the Delta community to help inform the recommendations of the Delta ISB on scientific issues important to management, including ecosystem restoration, water supply reliability, flood risk, water quality, and the Delta as an evolving place. As an Environmental Scientist, your expertise and research will help shape the next set of scientific reviews informing management decisions that affect the long-term health and resilience of the Delta.

We’re located in the new state of the art Natural Resources Building in downtown Sacramento. Our building features ergonomic furniture, panoramic downtown views, a free employee gym, a cafeteria and bodega, call and conference rooms, adjacent childcare, and much more.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Department Information**

The Delta Reform Act of 2009 created the Delta Stewardship Council (Council). The mission of the Council is to achieve the coequal goals of "...providing a more reliable water supply for California and protecting restoring and enhancing the Delta ecosystem... in a manner that protects and enhances the unique cultural, recreational, natural resource, and agricultural values of the Delta as an evolving place" (CA Water Code SS 85054). To do this, the Council developed the Delta Plan, which is an enforceable long-term sustainable management plan for the Delta to ensure coordinated action at the federal, state, and local levels.
  
  
The Council is devoted to fostering a culture of diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout all levels within our organization. The long-term success of the Council depends on our ability to promote a culture of creativity as we work toward our mandate comprised of co-equal goals. We hope to attract and retain employees by valuing and respecting their unique knowledge, life experiences, and backgrounds. The Council believes that our differences are what make us stronger as a team, and we encourage a culture that celebrates the unique attributes of all.

jobs.title: Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
Overview:

Are you a passionate about environmental stewardship? As the Environmental Specialist, you will provide technical input on environmental monitoring and design or construction methods to ensure compliance with environmental specifications or regulatory standards.

Bring your diverse ideas to build stronger, more resilient communities.

Apply now and transform your career with us.

What you will be doing:

* Audits, analyzes, and reports on environmental performance to internal and external clients, as well as regulatory bodies.
* Collaborates with design and construction teams to advise on minimizing adverse environmental impacts.
* Conducts impact assessments to identify, evaluate, and mitigate environmental risks and financial costs.
* Prepares environmental reports for supervisor review and leadership presentations.
* Raises awareness across the organization about emerging environmental issues and coordinates public hearings and consultations.
* Trains staff at all levels on environmental issues and responsibilities, and engages in environmental education and research to stay ahead of industry trends.

What we are looking for:

* Bachelor’s Degree in Environmental Science, Biology, or a related environmental field required.
* Environmental certification preferred.
* Experience in environmental monitoring preferred.

Why work for us:

Some of the benefits you may be eligible for as an employee are:

* Comprehensive compensation package and paid time off program
* Industry leading 401(k)/RRSP
* Medical/Extended Health Care, Dental, Vision and/or Provincial Medical
* Wellness benefits & Employee Assistance Program
* Tuition Reimbursement Program

We are an EEO/ADA/Veterans employer.

Salary Min: USD $78,000.00/Yr. Salary Max: USD $82,000.00/Yr.

Job Posting: Unit Chief

Department of Toxic Substances Control

JC-538910



Unit Chief
  
SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SUPERVISORY)

$10,854.00 - $13,493.00 per Month
  
New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**Final Filing Date:** **11/24/2026**

### **Job Description and Duties**

Are you an experienced leader looking for a rewarding technical career opportunity? This position supervises a multidisciplinary team of scientists, engineers and geologists responsible for resolving complex landfill projects. If you enjoy partnering with technical leads to developing effective solutions to challenging issues, we encourage you to apply!

  

**As a Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) you will have the opportunity to:**

* Provide direction and training to staff who oversee environmental investigations and cleanup activities at properties where hazardous materials, substances or waste were released into the environment
* Ensure that the requirements of legal mandates, which DTSC is party to, are implemented in an appropriate manner
* Provide guidance on staff’s review of submitted site cleanup related documents (e.g., Phase I, Preliminary Endangerment Assessment/Resource Conservation and Recovery Act Facility Assessment, Engineering Evaluation/Cost Analysis, Site Characterization work plans and reports, Remedial Investigation/ Feasibility Studies, Sampling and Analysis Plans, Human Health and Ecological Risk Assessment, etc.), field work oversight, regulatory decision making, and communication with responsible parties, project proponents, external agencies, and the public
* Monitor staff’s review of site cleanup-related documents for compliance with applicable standards and requirements, conduct oversight of field work consistent with DTSC approved work plans, and ensure remediation work meets federal and state standards
* Provide technical consultation and support to staff on most complex technical issues including investigations, data analysis, removal actions, remedial actions, and implementation of any repair, modification, or improvements to the site
* Oversee and assist staff in evaluating appropriate sampling and mitigation techniques, based on state of practice scientific and engineering practices, or as appropriate, uses innovative technologies to address unique and/or complex problems

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

**Effective July 1, 2025, specific Bargaining Units and associated Excluded State employees are subject to a salary reduction between 2% - 4.62% in exchange for hours in the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025) per month. For more details, please click here** https://hrmanual.calhr.ca.gov/Home/ManualItem/1/2113.

  

**This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship by the start date of employment. The Department of Toxic Substances Control does not participate in E-Verify for employment authorization purposes.**

  

**A hybrid schedule may be available for this position.**

Job Posting: Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory)

Department of Pesticide Regulation

JC-538755



Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory)
  
SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SUPERVISORY)

$10,854.00 - $13,493.00 per Month
  
New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**Final Filing Date:** **11/27/2026**

### **Job Description and Duties**

Are you interested in a meaningful and impactful career? Would you like to contribute to protecting people and the environment and accelerating a statewide transition to sustainable pest management? The Department of Pesticide Regulation (DPR) could be the place for you!
  
  
Under the general direction of the Environmental Program Manager I (Supervisory), the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) serves as the supervisor for professional scientific staff within the Department of Pesticide Regulation’s (DPR) Pesticide Use Reporting (PUR) Program. This position plans, directs, and evaluates scientific, technical, and programmatic activities supporting the accuracy, completeness, accessibility, and effective use of statewide pesticide use data. The Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) oversees PUR data quality and reporting activities, including quality assurance and quality control processes, development of the annual PUR report, responses to data requests, and technical support for urgent or complex data needs. The position provides technical and programmatic leadership on pesticide use reporting requirements, database and data system improvements, and changes resulting from legislation, regulation, and Department policy. The Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) supports implementation of Integrated Pest Management (IPM) Branch and Department priorities and follows direction and guidance provided by the Environmental Program Manager I (Supervisory), Branch Chief, and executive leadership.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

* Work primarily in an office building in a climate-controlled environment and under artificial lighting
* May be required to sit for long periods at a time
* Must be able to use a computer monitor, mouse, and keyboard for up to 8 hours per day
* Must be able to lift at least 10 pounds
* Occasional travel, sometimes requiring overnight stays, to conduct site visits or attend training events or workshops may be required.
* Site visits may require walking in agricultural fields and orchards and in natural areas with moderate slopes, unpaved grounds, and uneven surfaces, such as ploughed fields and grassy meadows, undeveloped roads, ditches, levees, and other structures located adjacent to agricultural fields. Site visits may also occur in urban and suburban environments. Site visits will occur under various climatic conditions that may require exposure to high heat, full sun, high humidity, wind, and rain.

  
**Note:** This position may be eligible for hybrid telework under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria set forth in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location, as indicated on their duty statement, at their own expense.
  
  
**Beginning July 1st, 2026, it is anticipated this position will be office-centered and employees will be expected to report to the office at least four days per week.**

Our core values include accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and integrity. We are innovative and passionate about the work we do.
  
  
DPR values diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout the organization. We foster an environment where employees from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. We believe the diversity of our employees is essential to inspiring innovative solutions. The Delta Reform Act of 2009 created the Delta Stewardship Council (Council). The mission of the Council is to achieve the coequal goals of "...providing a more reliable water supply for California and protecting restoring and enhancing the Delta ecosystem... in a manner that protects and enhances the unique cultural, recreational, natural resource, and agricultural values of the Delta as an evolving place" (CA Water Code SS 85054). To do this, the Council developed the Delta Plan, which is an enforceable long-term sustainable management plan for the Delta to ensure coordinated action at the federal, state, and local levels.
  
  
The Council is devoted to fostering a culture of diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout all levels within our organization. The long-term success of the Council depends on our ability to promote a culture of creativity as we work toward our mandate comprised of co-equal goals. We hope to attract and retain employees by valuing and respecting their unique knowledge, life experiences, and backgrounds. The Council believes that our differences are what make us stronger as a team, and we encourage a culture that celebrates the unique attributes of all.

### **Job Description and Duties**

Are you an experienced leader looking for a rewarding technical career opportunity? This position supervises a multidisciplinary team of scientists, engineers and geologists responsible for resolving complex landfill projects. If you enjoy partnering with technical leads to developing effective solutions to challenging issues, we encourage you to apply!

  

**As a Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) you will have the opportunity to:**

* Provide direction and training to staff who oversee environmental investigations and cleanup activities at properties where hazardous materials, substances or waste were released into the environment
* Ensure that the requirements of legal mandates, which DTSC is party to, are implemented in an appropriate manner
* Provide guidance on staff’s review of submitted site cleanup related documents (e.g., Phase I, Preliminary Endangerment Assessment/Resource Conservation and Recovery Act Facility Assessment, Engineering Evaluation/Cost Analysis, Site Characterization work plans and reports, Remedial Investigation/ Feasibility Studies, Sampling and Analysis Plans, Human Health and Ecological Risk Assessment, etc.), field work oversight, regulatory decision making, and communication with responsible parties, project proponents, external agencies, and the public
* Monitor staff’s review of site cleanup-related documents for compliance with applicable standards and requirements, conduct oversight of field work consistent with DTSC approved work plans, and ensure remediation work meets federal and state standards
* Provide technical consultation and support to staff on most complex technical issues including investigations, data analysis, removal actions, remedial actions, and implementation of any repair, modification, or improvements to the site
* Oversee and assist staff in evaluating appropriate sampling and mitigation techniques, based on state of practice scientific and engineering practices, or as appropriate, uses innovative technologies to address unique and/or complex problems

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.
